description: Expected behavior of the controlled Item 1A comparison workflow across five CONTROLLED SYNTHETIC fixture pairs. Every company here is fictional and every document is written or hand-assembled for this repository. This is a controlled regression suite that protects deterministic behavior from silent drift — it is NOT a real-filing benchmark, and no metric computed against it is evidence of accuracy on real SEC filings.
matching_semantics: A detected change matches an expected change iff (unit_key, change_type) are both equal, where unit_key is the detector's normalized heading slug (comparison_detector._slug) and the match is verified by recomputing the deterministic change_id. Changes the v3 detector serializes per unit under a sequence-aware identity (ambiguous duplicate-heading occurrences, identified as side:sequence:unit_key) are matched by listing those identities in the expected change's unit_identities and score under its unit_key. Undetermined and unlabeled detected changes count in the detected set and lower precision; they are never silently excluded. Aligned units whose content is identical emit no change (comparison.v1 has no 'unchanged' change type), so expected_unchanged_units assert ABSENCE.

fixtures.source: docs/ (the two controlled Acme 10-K excerpt fixtures, loaded through the real ingestion pipeline)
fixtures.scenario: Happy path: modified units, one added unit, one removed unit, and one byte-identical unchanged unit. Expectations are identical to tests/fixtures/comparison_item1a_labels.json, which the detector suite pins independently.

expected_changes.why: FY2025 adds two attempted intrusion events, raises cyber insurance from $35M to $50M, and reports zero-trust rollout complete.
FY2025 adds the December 2025 SEC AI-rule proposal and the March 2025 deficiency letter.
The AI and model risk factor exists only in the FY2025 filing, and both sections are proven complete.
The reference-rate transition risk factor exists only in the FY2024 filing, and both sections are proven complete.

expected_unchanged_units.why: The Item 1A introductory paragraph is byte-identical in both filings; it must align and must NOT be emitted as a change.

expected_release.why: Every validation check passes and no change is undetermined, so policy determined review was not required. Release does not require a human approval and must not be routed through a fake one.

fixtures.scenario: Item 1A is byte-identical across periods. Zero changes must be emitted and no unit may become a false positive.

expected_unchanged_units.why: Identical introductory text on both sides.
Identical unit text on both sides.
Identical unit text on both sides; also proves reconstruction across two chunks does not manufacture a difference.

expected_release.why: A comparison that found no changes is valid and carries no failed or undetermined validation, so policy returns it.

fixtures.scenario: The current filing is indexed but has no resolvable Item 1A section. The outcome must be ONE undetermined section-level change — never two 'removed' changes for the previous filing's two units.

expected_changes.why: Data insufficiency yields an undetermined RESULT (status 'detected'), not a failed comparison, and absence of a section can never be reported as removed risk factors.

expected_release.why: An undetermined change is a mandatory-hold condition, so the pending held result is not release-eligible. Only an approved terminal review makes it eligible, and the export must then carry the final reviewed snapshot.

fixtures.scenario: The current filing repeats a normalized risk-factor heading. Alignment for that key is ambiguous and must stay undetermined rather than guessing a pairing; every occurrence of the repeated heading is serialized as its own undetermined change under a sequence-aware unit identity, never collapsed into one change per heading key.

expected_changes.why: The heading key is not unique within the current filing, so all three of its units (one previous, two current) are excluded from pairing and each is reported as its own undetermined change under its sequence-aware unit identity.

expected_unchanged_units.why: Identical introductory text on both sides; ambiguity elsewhere must not disturb it.

expected_release.why: A rejected terminal review is a human decision that the output must not be released; the governed snapshot is preserved verbatim and no export may be produced.

fixtures.scenario: One risk factor is retitled AND substantially reworded.

expected_changes.why: Documented v1 limitation: heading alignment is exact and the content-hash fallback requires an EXACT normalized content match, so a retitled-and-reworded unit does not pair.
The other half of the same documented limitation: the retitled unit surfaces as added rather than modified.

expected_unchanged_units.why: Identical introductory text on both sides.

expected_release.why: The added/removed pair is evidence-backed and every check passes, so policy returns it. The suite labels the SEMANTIC limitation honestly instead of relaxing the detector: a human reader would call this one modified risk factor.

fixtures.limitation: comparison.v1 has deliberately no similarity stage. A reworded-and-retitled risk factor is reported as an added+removed pair, not as one modified unit. This label pins the current contract; changing it requires changing the detector deliberately, in its own commit, with this label updated in the same reviewed diff.
